lead: The largest fresh-produce market in Europe. A Modernist cathedral of iron, stained glass and tiles where the aromas of the huerta and the Mediterranean fill every corner since 1928.

On the same site where travelling markets were held since the city’s first medieval expansion, the Central Market of Valencia has operated without interruption since its opening on 23 January 1928. Its Modernist architecture — designed for 959 stalls — was conceived as a tribute to the agricultural potential of the Valencian huerta, and is today considered the “cathedral of the senses”: the light coming in through the stained glass, the permanent murmur and the explosion of colours and aromas make every visit a unique experience.

Admission to the market is completely free. It opens Monday to Saturday from 7:30 to 15:00 and closes on Sundays and public holidays. To experience it fully, come on a weekday first thing in the morning.

items.kicker: Site of Cultural Interest · Valencian Modernism
items.title: The Dome and Modernist Architecture
items.subtitle: Wrought iron · Tiles · Stained glass · 30 m dome
items.body: The Central Market building is one of the most spectacular and most visited constructions in Valencia. Designed by the architects Alejandro Soler March and Francisco Guardia Vial — trained at the Barcelona School of Architecture and collaborators of Lluís Domènech i Montaner —, it was built between 1914 and 1928. Its Modernist architecture is a tribute to the agricultural potential of the Valencian huerta. The central dome of iron, glass and ceramics reaches 30 metres in height and is crowned by the famous parrot weathervane, a symbol of the market’s hustle and bustle. The polychrome stained glass bathes the interior in magical light, creating one of the most photographed settings in Valencia.
facts: Alejandro Soler March and Francisco Guardia Vial · Barcelona School
1914–1928 · Opened on 23 January 1928 by Alfonso XIII
30 metres high · Iron, glass and ceramics · Crowned by the parrot
Site of Cultural Interest · The largest Modernist market in Europe

items.title: More than 250 Fresh-Produce Stalls
items.subtitle: 8,000 m² · Produce from the Valencian Huerta and the Mediterranean
items.body: With more than 250 active stalls spread over 8,000 m², the Central Market is the largest fresh-produce market in Europe. The colours and aromas of its stalls run through every section: poultry, butchery, charcuterie, spices, fruit, nuts, gourmet, bakery and pastry, fish and seafood, salted fish and pickles, and international products. Local produce dominates the counters: the Valencian huerta, the Mediterranean Sea and local producers are the great protagonists. Many stalls offer products with a Designation of Origin of the Comunitat Valenciana.
facts: Poultry, butchery, charcuterie, spices, fruit, nuts, bakery, fish, salted fish, gourmet

items.title: Central Bar · Ricard Camarena
items.subtitle: The restaurant of the Michelin-starred chef in the heart of the market
items.body: The Central Bar is the best-known food venue inside the Central Market, run by the Valencian chef Ricard Camarena, one of the most acclaimed cooks in Spain and a Michelin-starred chef. The concept combines the tradition of the market bar with signature cooking: tapas, raciones and sandwiches with ingredients bought directly from the market’s vendors, prepared on the spot. The space occupies a strategic corner of the building and has an indoor terrace under the stained glass. It is essential for the Valencian esmorzaret or for a quality lunch after strolling past the stalls.
facts: Ricard Camarena · Michelin star · Cook of the year

items.title: Typical Valencian Products to Take Home
items.subtitle: Valencian rice · Tiger nuts · Saffron · Turrón · DO wines · Horchata
items.body: The Central Market is the best place in Valencia to take home the authentic flavours of the city. Valencian rice is sold in its three Designation of Origin varieties: Senia, Bomba and Albufera. Valencia tiger nuts — with their own DO — are the ingredient of horchata, an Arab drink popularised in the city. Saffron, spices, artisan turrón, vacuum-packed salted fish, cured ham, olives and DO Valencia wines complete the shop window. You will also find Valencian ceramics and paellas — the pans — of all sizes among the most authentic souvenirs.
facts: Senia, Bomba and Albufera · The three Valencian rice varieties

items.title: Surroundings · La Lonja de la Seda and the Church of the Santos Juanes
items.subtitle: Plaza del Mercado · Three monuments face to face
items.body: The location of the Central Market in the Plaza del Mercado creates one of the most singular monumental ensembles in the city: face to face with La Lonja de la Seda — a World Heritage Site — and flanked by the Church of the Santos Juanes, with its Baroque façade. The three buildings have shared the same square for centuries and create a unique architectural setting in which the market’s Modernism converses with the civil Gothic of the 15th century and the Baroque of the 17th. From the Plaza del Mercado you can also easily reach El Carmen and Ruzafa.
facts: La Lonja de la Seda · World Heritage Site (UNESCO, 1996)

blocks.title: Tips for visiting the Central Market
items: The market closes on Sundays and public holidays — check the opening hours before you go
On weekdays at 8:00 or 9:00 there is the widest choice and the fewest people
Ricard Camarena’s Central Bar fills up fast: arrive early if you want a place for the esmorzaret
DO Valencia rice (Senia, Bomba and Albufera) is the best food souvenir you can take home
La Lonja de la Seda is right opposite — combine the market visit with admission to the UNESCO monument
You can buy online or via WhatsApp from the market’s vendors with home delivery
